_meta.title: C2PA Compatibility List
_meta.description: Canonical JSON source for cameras, smartphones, apps, platforms, and tools that support C2PA Content Credentials.

Leica.name: M11-P
Leica.notes: The world's first camera with built-in Content Credentials, using a dedicated hardware chip to sign images at the moment of capture.

Leica.name: M11-D
Leica.notes: The second Leica camera to integrate C2PA-compliant authenticity technology, continuing the focus on verifiable provenance.

Leica.name: SL3
Leica.notes: Does not support C2PA. Leica has stated that firmware-only solutions do not meet its security standards for encryption.

Sony.name: Alpha 1 (a1)
Sony.notes: C2PA support added via firmware update (Ver. 2.00), enabling in-camera digital signatures to authenticate images.

Sony.name: Alpha 9 III (a9 III)
Sony.notes: Support for C2PA image authenticity was included in a firmware update (Ver. 2.00).

Sony.name: Alpha 7S III (a7S III)
Sony.notes: Firmware update (Ver. 3.00) brought Sony's Camera Authenticity Solution to this model.

Sony.name: Alpha 7 IV (a7 IV)
Sony.notes: Gained C2PA support through a firmware update (Ver. 3.00), embedding provenance metadata directly into files.

Nikon.name: Z9
Nikon.notes: Nikon showed a Z9 provenance prototype in 2022, but Nikon's current Authenticity Service still publicly lists only the Z6III as compatible; no public Z9 rollout is documented as of May 4, 2026.

Nikon.name: Z6 III
Nikon.notes: Supports Nikon Authenticity Service with C2PA Content Credentials; Nikon says Z6III compatibility is live as of August 27, 2025 and requires Nikon Imaging Cloud plus current firmware.

Canon.name: EOS R1
Canon.notes: Supports C2PA content authentication, initially available for registered news agencies to verify image authenticity from capture.

Canon.name: EOS R5 Mark II
Canon.notes: Firmware update added C2PA support, embedding verifiable metadata to help combat misinformation.

Fujifilm.name: GFX100S II
Fujifilm.notes: Reported to have C2PA support for embedding content provenance information.

Fujifilm.name: X-T50
Fujifilm.notes: Reported to be a C2PA-compliant device, allowing creators to attach authenticity data to their images.

Samsung.name: Galaxy S25 Series
Samsung.notes: The industry's first smartphone lineup to natively support C2PA Content Credentials, initially for images created or edited with Galaxy AI.

Samsung.name: Galaxy Devices (via Gallery App)
Samsung.notes: A Gallery app update is rolling out Content Credentials support to more Galaxy devices, showing a 'CR' icon for details on AI edits.

Google.name: Pixel 10
Google.notes: Google says Pixel 10 is the first phone with C2PA Content Credentials across every photo created by Pixel Camera; Google Photos can also display credentials.

Hardware Enablers.name: Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 3
Hardware Enablers.notes: This mobile platform integrates C2PA support at the chip level in partnership with Truepic, enabling any smartphone manufacturer to adopt the standard.

Adobe.name: Photoshop
Adobe.notes: Allows creators to attach Content Credentials during export, providing a transparent edit history.

Adobe.name: Lightroom (CC & Classic)
Adobe.notes: Supports attaching Content Credentials to JPEG files on export, logging edits and creator information.

Adobe.name: Fresco
Adobe.notes: Allows artists to export their work with Content Credentials, which can then be displayed on platforms like Behance.

Capture One.name: Capture One Pro (Studio & All in One)
Capture One.notes: Introduced in Capture One 16.5.0 and still beta as of March 10, 2026. Available in All in One and Studio, appending edit history on JPEG/TIFF export while preserving existing credentials.

OpenAI.name: DALL-E 3
OpenAI.notes: Automatically embeds C2PA metadata into generated images to clearly label them as AI-created.

OpenAI.name: Sora
OpenAI.notes: OpenAI says all Sora videos embed C2PA metadata, and OpenAI Media Service appears on the C2PA Conforming Products List as of January 28, 2026.

Microsoft.name: Bing Image Creator
Microsoft.notes: All images generated with this tool include an invisible C2PA digital watermark, confirming their AI provenance.

Microsoft.name: Designer
Microsoft.notes: Microsoft documents that Designer includes C2PA-based content credentials for AI-generated and AI-edited images, with controls for embedding credentials on export.

Adobe.name: Firefly
Adobe.notes: All content generated with Adobe Firefly automatically includes Content Credentials, indicating its AI origin.

Google.name: Imagen (in Vertex AI & Products)
Google.notes: Google's image generation models are being updated to include C2PA metadata, which surfaces in features like 'About this image' in Google Search.

Adobe.name: Behance
Adobe.notes: Natively displays the 'CR' icon for Content Credentials, allowing viewers to inspect an asset's creation and edit history.

Adobe.name: Adobe Stock
Adobe.notes: Preserves and displays Content Credentials for supported assets, providing transparency for stock media.

Social Media.name: LinkedIn
Social Media.notes: Displays a 'CR' icon on images with attached Content Credentials, giving users access to provenance information directly in their feed.

Social Media.name: TikTok
Social Media.notes: The first social platform to automatically apply Content Credentials labels to AI-generated content uploaded to its platform, enhancing transparency.

Search Engines.name: Google Search
Search Engines.notes: The 'About this image' feature can read and display C2PA metadata, helping users get context on images they find online.

Search Engines.name: Microsoft Bing
Search Engines.notes: Features like 'About this image' are being implemented to provide provenance information for images, leveraging C2PA standards.

Content Authenticity Initiative.name: Content Credentials Verify
Content Authenticity Initiative.notes: The official web-based tool for inspecting any media file to see if it contains Content Credentials and to view its full history.

Truepic.name: Truepic Lens & SDKs
Truepic.notes: Provides enterprise-level tools and SDKs for securely capturing and verifying digital photos and videos using the C2PA standard.

Independent.name: C2PA Viewer
Independent.notes: A third-party tool and website dedicated to making C2PA information easy to view and understand for the general public.
